title: Planning versus improvising: Coltrane and Andrew Hill's lead sheets
summary: Some music was shaped on the bandstand; Coltrane's quartet rehearsed, and Andrew Hill gave only a guidepost lead sheet, important to Tolliver's career.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young

blocks.x: I wondered on occasion if the musicians like yourself and the fellas you mentioned sat around and talked about how they were going to play. Was there discussions that said like we might say, all right, we’re not going to play in this particular time signature, we’re just going to see what happens? Or I guess what I’m trying to say was any of this music pre-planned before you got on the bandstand or did it happen as it was being created?

I would imagine some of it did happen as it was being created, that whoever was the band leader said, you know, this is, you know, these couple of notes or whatever, maybe. Let’s just work off of that and, you know, see what we get. You know John Coltrane, I mean we all got a chance to watch that develop you know, from the beginning when he put that quartet together, finally, who were going to be in it for that run ‘til his death. And they rehearsed you know. And when it got to the point when he decided he wanted to go interstellar I think he probably gave a couple of notes you know, to work off of, to McCoy and off they went. I mean in that case, where you have a band where each instrumentalist in the band is creating a path that’s going to be historical, then young players pick up on that and if they want to do that they probably say I want this to go something like on that record or on this record you know. But I worked with Andrew Hill, Andrew scripted out a lead sheet. But he never said okay you have to play it this way or that way. It was really just a guidepost. Because he expected you to take it and do how you wanted to do with it.
That was a, you know, my experience with Andrew Hill was very important in my career because of how he handled what you’re asking about.
